newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SembCorp, MRT may bid for telecom licence.
newsitem.headline: SembCorp, MRT may bid for telecom licence.

text.p: SembCorp Ltd and Singapore MRT Ltd said on Monday they were contemplating bidding for a public basic telecommunication services licence in Singapore.
The companies said in a joint statement they were considering acting together in consortium to form the local Singapore partners for such a bid.

"The consortium is curently evaluating the terms and conditions as well as the overall feasibility of bidding for the licence. The consortium is also in discussion with potential foreign telephone companies who may be invited to joint the consortium in the bid," the statement said.

Singapore plans to open up its telecoms market to competition from April, 2000, and has said it will allow one or two groups to compete directly with the current monopoly, Singapore Telecommunications Ltd from that date.
SembCorp and Singapore MRT, which is owned by state investment company Temasek Holdings, are the third group of companies to signal their interest in bidding for the licence.

On March 13, British Telecom, Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp and two Temasek-owned companies, state utility Singapore Power and Singapore Technologies Telemedia, said they formed a consortium to bid for a licence.
Singapore Press Holdings and Keppel Telecom have also said they want to bid in partnership, as has Britain's Cable & Wireless and its unit Hong Kong Telecommunications.
